title.narrative: Ebola Early Action: Outbreak Response & Mitigation in Uganda

description.narrative: On 30 January 2025, the Ministry of Health (MoH) declared an Ebola Virus Disease outbreak caused by the Sudan virus following laboratory confirmation of a case from three national reference laboratories. This is the eight Ebola outbreak in Uganda since 2000. The index case developed symptoms on 19 January 2025 and succumbed to the illness on 29 January at Mulago National Referral Hospital in Kampala. As of 4 February 2025, there were seven (07) confirmed cases, including one (01) death. Among them, four (57%) are health workers, while three (43%) are family members. A total of 289 contacts have been listed, with 154 in the Kampala Metropolitan Area. Women and girls account for 57% of reported cases, and children make up over 14%. Contacts are distributed across Kampala (154), Mbale (104), and Jinja (31). As of 12 February, the number of confirmed infections has increased to nine (09), though the number of fatalities remains at one (01). The Sudan Virus Disease is a severe hemorrhagic fever from the same family as the Ebola Virus, with a case fatality rate of 41% to 70%. No licensed vaccines or therapeutics currently exist for its prevention or treatment, posing a significant public health threat. However, vaccine trials against SVD are currently underway in Kampala. This marks Uganda’s eighth Ebola outbreak, the most recent occurring in 2022, which was successfully contained in 69 days. Uganda has the capacity to respond effectively, provided there is timely technical and financial support.
